# Time Series Advanced {.center}

## Topics Covered

- STL decomposition (trend/seasonal)
- Forecasting with ARIMA
- Prophet models
- Change point detection
- Spectral analysis (FFT)

Goal: Advanced temporal patterns

## Setup

Data: monthly dengue cases from 30 city wards, 2023–2025 (`data/dengue_wards.csv`, simulated; see `data/README.md`).
A trial with three visits is not a time series: these methods need many equally spaced time points.

```{r}
#| echo: true
library(tidyverse); library(forecast)
dengue <- read_csv("../../data/dengue_wards.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
monthly <- dengue |>
  group_by(month_index) |>                                   # 36 consecutive months
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), rain_mm = mean(rain_mm), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(date = seq(as.Date("2023-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n()))
cases_ts <- ts(monthly$cases, start = c(2023, 1), frequency = 12)
```

## STL Decomposition

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "STL decomposition of monthly dengue cases into the data, a trend, a seasonal pattern peaking in mid-year, and the remainder."
stl_result <- stl(log1p(cases_ts), s.window = "periodic")
autoplot(stl_result) +
  labs(title = "STL decomposition of monthly dengue cases (log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Separates the **trend**, the **seasonal** pattern (a peak every monsoon) and the **remainder**.
The log scale makes the seasonal swing additive.

## Forecasting with ARIMA

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Monthly dengue cases 2023 to 2025 with a 12-month seasonal ARIMA forecast for 2026 and its 80% and 95% prediction bands."
arima_model <- auto.arima(cases_ts, lambda = 0)       # lambda = 0: model the log, forecast on the case scale
forecast_result <- forecast(arima_model, h = 12)
autoplot(forecast_result) +
  labs(title = "12-month dengue forecast (seasonal ARIMA)", x = NULL, y = "Cases per month") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Dark band = 80%, light band = 95% prediction interval. Three seasons are a short history:
the bands are wide, and that is the honest message.

## Prophet Forecasting

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Prophet fit to monthly dengue cases with points for the data, a line for the fitted values and a shaded uncertainty band extending 12 months ahead."
library(prophet)
m <- prophet(data.frame(ds = monthly$date, y = log1p(monthly$cases)),
             yearly.seasonality = TRUE, weekly.seasonality = FALSE, daily.seasonality = FALSE)
future <- make_future_dataframe(m, periods = 12, freq = "month")
fc <- predict(m, future)
plot(m, fc) + labs(title = "Prophet forecast (log cases)", x = NULL, y = "log(1 + cases)")
```

Prophet fits a trend plus yearly seasonality; it is easy to use but, like any model, only as good as the history.

## Change Point Detection

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Monthly dengue cases with red horizontal segments showing the mean level between the change points found by PELT."
library(changepoint)
y <- as.numeric(log1p(cases_ts))
noise_sd <- mad(diff(y)) / sqrt(2)                   # cpt.mean() assumes a noise SD of 1: rescale first
cpt_result <- cpt.mean(y / noise_sd, method = "PELT")
plot(cpt_result, cpt.col = "red", cpt.width = 3, ylab = "log(1 + cases) / noise SD", xlab = "Month (1 = Jan 2023)",
     main = "Change points in the mean level")
cpts(cpt_result)
```

Here the "changes" are the start and end of each season: a change-point method finds **level shifts**,
so remove the seasonal pattern first if you are looking for a shift in the underlying trend.

## Rolling Statistics Plot

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-alt: "Monthly dengue cases in grey with a 3-month rolling mean in blue and a shaded band of plus or minus one rolling standard deviation."
library(zoo)
rolling <- monthly |>
  mutate(roll_mean = rollmean(cases, k = 3, fill = NA),
         roll_sd = rollapply(cases, width = 3, FUN = sd, fill = NA))
ggplot(rolling, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cases), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = roll_mean - roll_sd, ymax = roll_mean + roll_sd), alpha = 0.2, fill = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = roll_mean), colour = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "3-month rolling mean ± SD", x = NULL, y = "Cases per month") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Summary

**Advanced time series:**

1. STL decomposition - separate components
2. ARIMA forecasting - statistical predictions
3. Prophet - flexible, interpretable forecasts
4. Change points - detect regime shifts
5. Rolling statistics - smoothed trends
